what: C.H. Robinson arranges freight. It books truck, rail, ocean and air capacity on behalf of shippers without owning the vehicles, and handles customs and supply chain management.
customers: Manufacturers, retailers and distributors moving freight across North America and internationally.
money: ocean and air freight forwarding and customs
moat: A network of relationships with tens of thousands of carriers and shippers, plus pricing data from millions of shipments, which lets it match capacity faster than smaller brokers.
risks: Freight brokerage margins compress when truckload capacity is abundant
Revenue has fallen about 13% a year over three years
Digital brokers compete on technology and price
Freight volumes have been weak for three years
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 20% with no assets to depreciate
Analysts see about 31% upside from current levels
Cost reduction and automation have lifted productivity per employee substantially
watch: Adjusted gross profit per transaction and truckload volumes.
